SMTO-FIL-0037 — The Gateway is handling too many file copies right now

GUID: 4a39d4f9-c926-4341-8f34-f0fa34d5987a
Slug: file-transfer-capacity
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • The Gateway computer is already tracking as many file copies as it can, including unfinished ones it still has to clean up. SMTO stopped this copy before sending any of the file.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look in your conversations for other Tasks that are copying files to or from the same Gateway, and let them finish. Each running copy takes one of the Gateway's limited copy slots.
  2. Wait about five minutes. The Gateway frees slots from copies that have stopped being used after about five minutes.
  3. Ask SMTO to check that the file isn't already at the destination, then ask it to copy again, one file at a time if you were copying many. Checking first avoids a duplicate, and fewer copies at once keeps the Gateway under its limit.

What success looks like

  • The copy starts and SMTO reports the file was copied and verified.

If it still fails

  • If it keeps happening after waiting, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway; unfinished copies may be stuck waiting for cleanup. Don't start many copies at once to get around the limit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway refused a new transfer because its active session table is at MAX_SESSIONS (16), or its transfer journal holds 256 records with no cleaned committed, verified or aborted record that can be evicted.

What this means

  • The active session table is full, or the durable journal is full and has no terminal fully cleaned record eligible for eviction. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The active session table is full, or the durable journal is full and has no terminal fully cleaned record eligible for eviction.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect active sessions and unresolved journal cleanup; do not delete recovery evidence to free slots.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the Gateway's transfer journal (transfers records for the node) and log for 'Transfer cleanup incomplete' warnings. Let active sessions finish or expire (300 s idle), resolve records left with cleanup_complete false or state committing/unknown, and reduce concurrent copies to that Gateway.
  • Wait for existing transfers to release capacity or reduce concurrent transfer work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Existing owned work settles and the normal lifecycle releases capacity.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
